overview: The School Committee recognized state legislators for passing the Student Opportunity Act, approved continuing the districtwide universal free breakfast pilot, and honored outgoing Mayor Stephanie Muccini Burke and committee members Erin DiBenedetto and Michael Ruggiero.

items.title: Holiday Musical Performance
items.summary: The Medford High School string ensemble performed holiday musical selections for the committee.

items.title: Approval of Minutes and Bills
items.summary: The committee approved the minutes of December 9, 2019, as amended, and approved the transfer of funds.

items.title: Special Education Subcommittee Report
items.summary: The committee accepted the Special Education Subcommittee report on disability awareness training, summer recreation access, and future programming goals.

items.title: Recognition of State Delegation for the Student Opportunity Act
items.summary: The committee and administration presented commemorative school bells to Senator Patricia Jehlen and Representatives Paul Donato, Christine Barber, and Sean Garballey for their advocacy on the Student Opportunity Act.

items.title: Veterans Day Commemoration Report
items.summary: Dr. Nicole Chiesa reported on the high school's 19th annual Veterans Day speaker program and the student-led Veterans Preservation Project, and the committee placed the report on file.

items.title: Universal Breakfast Program Update
items.summary: Following a report showing a 6,000-meal increase in participation, the committee voted to continue the Provision 2 free breakfast program for all schools through the remainder of the school year.

items.title: Condolence Resolutions
items.summary: The committee observed a moment of silence and adopted resolutions of condolence for retired Police Sergeant Cesar Della Torre and former School Committee member Lina DiGiantomaso.

items.title: Recognition of Outgoing Committee Members
items.summary: The committee, administration, and state delegation recognized outgoing Mayor Stephanie Muccini Burke, Erin DiBenedetto, and Michael Ruggiero for their years of public service.
